theorem_title: Eventual volume bound and vanishing shape imply an exponential margin
formal_statement:
namespace ZetaNine

theorem exponential_margin_of_volume_and_shape (B σ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hB : ∃ β : ℝ, β < (2641 / 250 : ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop, B (2 * k + 2) ≤ β)
    (hS : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => σ (2 * k + 2))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
      ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
        B (2 * k + 2) + σ (2 * k + 2) ≤ (2641 / 250 : ℝ) - ε := by sorry

end ZetaNine
natural_language_statement: For arbitrary real sequences B and σ, suppose B(2k+2) is eventually at most some β<2641/250 and σ(2k+2) tends to zero. Then some positive ε gives B(2k+2)+σ(2k+2)≤2641/250−ε for all sufficiently large k. This is the abstract V+S⇒J bridge; it does not establish those hypotheses for the concrete ζ(9) sequences.
source: Local ζ(9) roadmap/DAG.md §V and S to J; mathematical proof in notes, Lean statement only in this draft.

readback.readback: For any functions \(B,\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\), suppose there is a real number \(\beta<2641/250\) such that \(B(2k+2)\leq\beta\) for all sufficiently large natural numbers \(k\), and suppose \(\sigma(2k+2)\to 0\) as \(k\to\infty\). Then there is a real number \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(B(2k+2)+\sigma(2k+2)\leq 2641/250-\varepsilon\) for all sufficiently large natural numbers \(k\). The hypotheses impose no conditions on the functions at indices outside the sequence \(2,4,6,\ldots\).
